lines: Expo Router supports three output targets for web apps.

-| Output             | Expo Router | API Routes  | Description                                                                                                                                                                      |

-| `single` (default) | <YesIcon /> | <NoIcon />  | Outputs a Single Page Application (SPA) with a single **index.html** in the output directory and has no statically indexable HTML.                                               |

-| `server`           | <YesIcon /> | <YesIcon /> | Creates **client** and **server** directories. Client files are output as separate HTML files. API routes as separate JavaScript files for hosting with a custom Node.js server. |

-| `static`           | <YesIcon /> | <NoIcon />  | Outputs separate HTML files for every route in the **app** directory.                                                                                                            |

+| Output             | Expo Router | API Routes         | Description                                                                                                                                                                      |

+| `single` (default) | <YesIcon /> | <NoIcon />         | Outputs a Single Page Application (SPA) with a single **index.html** in the output directory and has no statically indexable HTML.                                               |

+| `server`           | <YesIcon /> | Enabled by default | Creates **client** and **server** directories. Client files are output as separate HTML files. API routes as separate JavaScript files for hosting with a custom Node.js server. |

+| `static`           | <YesIcon /> | Opt-in             | Outputs separate HTML files for every route in the **app** directory.                                                                                                            |

+In SDK 58 and later, set `apiRoutes: true` in the `expo-router` config plugin to enable API routes with `static` output. API routes are enabled by default with `server` output. Set `apiRoutes: false` to disable them in either mode. See [API routes](/router/web/api-routes/#create-an-api-route) for configuration and deployment requirements.
> **info** **Note**: For `static` and `server` output modes, you can configure [global HTTP headers](/router/web/server-headers) that are applied to all route responses via the `expo-router` plugin.

+In SDK 58 and later, API routes are enabled by default with `web.output: "server"`. To combine API routes with HTML generated at build time, use `web.output: "static"` and enable `apiRoutes` in the `expo-router` config plugin:
+This exports prerendered HTML and API routes to **dist/server**, and client assets to **dist/client**. It requires a [deployed server](#deployment).

+Set `apiRoutes` to `false` to disable API routes while keeping your selected rendering mode. Enabling API routes requires `static` or `server` output. An explicit `apiRoutes: false` is accepted in any output mode.
